docs.title: ANPR (Automatic Number Plate Recognition) Implementation
docs.text: Complete ANPR system for MIA vehicle telemetry platform with Czech license plate detection and edalnice.cz integration.

docs.title: 🎯 Features
docs.text:
• License Plate Detection: Real-time OCR for vehicle license plates using EasyOCR
  • Czech Plate Recognition: Optimized for Czech plate format (2 letters + 3-5 digits + 2 letters)
  • Vehicle Status Checking: Electronic vignette and exemption status from edalnice.gov.cz (services/edalnice_client.py; optional EDALNICE_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS, live validation tracked in #123)
  • Live Alert System: Real-time notifications for exempted vehicles ("Vozidlo osvobozeno")
  • WebSocket Streaming: Real-time plate detection stream to Android app
  • Local Caching: Intelligent caching of edalnice.cz lookups (24h TTL)
  • Image Preprocessing: Contrast enhancement for improved OCR accuracy

docs.title: 1. Backend Dependencies (RPi)
docs.text:
Install Python ANPR packages:

cd /home/sparrow/projects/mia

# Install new dependencies
pip install easyocr opencv-python Pillow

# Verify installation
python -c "import easyocr; import cv2; print('ANPR dependencies OK')"

docs.title: 2. Backend Integration
docs.text:
The ANPR router is already integrated into FastAPI:

# Added to apps/rpi-backend/py-api/api/main.py
from api.routers.anpr import router as anpr_router
app.include_router(anpr_router)

docs.title: Hardware Requirements
docs.text:
• ESP32-CAM with OV2640 camera
  • USB-to-UART adapter for programming
  • 5V power supply (>1A)

docs.text:
cd /home/sparrow/projects/mia/apps/esp32

# Build with PlatformIO
pio run -e esp32cam-anpr -t upload

# Or configure WiFi and compile

# - Line 31: WIFI_SSID = "Your WiFi SSID"
# - Line 32: WIFI_PASSWORD = "Your WiFi Password"  
# - Line 33: BACKEND_URL = "http://YOUR_BACKEND_IP:8000"

# Configure backend control path (used by POST /anpr/capture)
export ANPR_CAMERA_URL="http://ESP32_CAMERA_IP"

docs.title: 📊 Database Schema (Future)
docs.text:
When database integration is added:

-- License plate scans
CREATE TABLE license_plate_scans (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    plate_text VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    confidence FLOAT NOT NULL,
    device_id VARCHAR(50),
    image_path VARCHAR(255),
    image_hash VARCHAR(64) UNIQUE
);

-- Scan results (edalnice.cz lookups)
CREATE TABLE scan_results (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    scan_id INTEGER REFERENCES license_plate_scans(id),
    vehicle_info JSONB,
    edalnice_status VARCHAR(50),
    is_exempted BOOLEAN,
    exemption_reason TEXT,
    alert_sent BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    checked_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    expires_at TIMESTAMP  -- Cache expiration
);

-- Alerts
CREATE TABLE anpr_alerts (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    plate VARCHAR(20),
    alert_type VARCHAR(50),  -- 'exempted', 'debt', 'not_found'
    message TEXT,
    alert_sent_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    driver_id VARCHAR(50)
);

docs.title: 🔐 Privacy & Security
docs.text:
• Image Storage: Images are processed in-memory only, not persisted
  • Plate Data Retention: Plate text stored for 30 days max, then auto-deleted
  • API Authentication: Integrate with existing auth system for production
  • edalnice.cz Cache: 24-hour TTL prevents excessive API calls
  • SSL/TLS: Use HTTPS in production environment

docs.title: Issue: OCR accuracy is low
docs.text: Solution: 1. Improve lighting in test environment 2. Increase JPEG quality (change JPEG_QUALITY to 90) 3. Adjust image preprocessing (line 150-170 in anpr_service.py) 4. Check plate image is 640x480 or larger

docs.title: Issue: edalnice.cz API timeout
docs.text: Solution: Already handled with 5-second timeout and fallback to "unknown" status

docs.title: ANPR Quick Start Guide
docs.text: Get your ANPR system up and running in 30 minutes.

docs.title: Step 1: Install Backend Dependencies (5 minutes)
docs.text:
cd /home/sparrow/projects/mia

# Install ANPR packages (optional extras, not in requirements.txt)
pip install -r requirements-anpr.txt

# Verify
python -c "import easyocr; import cv2; print('✓ ANPR ready')"

docs.title: Step 2: Start Backend API (5 minutes)
docs.text:
# Terminal 1: Start ZeroMQ broker
cd /home/sparrow/projects/mia
python -m apps.rpi_backend.shared.messaging.broker

# Terminal 2: Start FastAPI server
cd /home/sparrow/projects/mia
PYTHONPATH=apps/rpi-backend/py-api python -m uvicorn api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload

You should see: 

INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000

docs.title: Complete Flow
docs.text:
ESP32 Camera captures image
    ↓
Sends to Backend API (/anpr/process)
    ↓
Backend runs OCR → Detects plate
    ↓
Backend checks edalnice.cz → Gets status
    ↓
Broadcasts via WebSocket → Android app receives
    ↓
Android displays result with alert if exempted

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
• Faster OCR: Reduce confidence threshold to 0.5 (faster, less accurate)
  • Better Accuracy: Increase confidence threshold to 0.8 (slower, more accurate)
  • Continuous Capture: ESP32 captures every 5 seconds (adjustable in firmware)
  • Batch Processing: Send multiple images for better throughput
  • Caching: edalnice.cz results cached for 24 hours

docs.title: WS /ws
docs.text:
WebSocket endpoint for real-time telemetry streaming.

Connection: ws://<raspberry-pi-ip>:8000/ws

Message Format (Server → Client): 

{
  "type": "telemetry",
  "data": {
    "device-1": {
      "temperature": 25.5,
      "humidity": 60.0
    }
  },
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"
}

Update Frequency: 10Hz (100ms intervals)

Example (JavaScript): 

const ws = new WebSocket('ws://192.168.1.100:8000/ws');

ws.onmessage = (event) => {
  const data = JSON.parse(event.data);
  console.log('Telemetry:', data);
};

ws.onerror = (error) => {
  console.error('WebSocket error:', error);
};

Example (Python): 

import asyncio
import websockets
import json

async def listen_telemetry():
    uri = "ws://192.168.1.100:8000/ws"
    async with websockets.connect(uri) as websocket:
        while True:
            message = await websocket.recv()
            data = json.loads(message)
            print(f"Telemetry: {data}")

asyncio.run(listen_telemetry())

const configResponse = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/gpio/configure`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ pin: 18, direction: 'output' })
});
console.log(await configResponse.json());

// Set GPIO
const setResponse = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/gpio/set`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ pin: 18, value: true })
});
console.log(await setResponse.json());

docs.title: Integration with ZeroMQ
docs.text:
The API acts as a bridge between HTTP/REST and the ZeroMQ messaging system. All commands are forwarded to the ZeroMQ broker, which routes them to appropriate workers.

See ZeroMQ Message Formats for details on the underlying message protocol.

docs.title: ARM64 Build Requirements and Setup Guide
docs.text: This document outlines the specific requirements and procedures for building the MIA project on ARM64 platforms (Raspberry Pi 4/5, Apple Silicon Macs, ARM servers).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The MIA project supports ARM64 architecture with both native compilation and cross-compilation workflows. The build system uses Conan for dependency management and CMake for build configuration.

docs.title: Primary Target: Raspberry Pi
docs.text:
• Raspberry Pi 4B/5: Primary deployment target
  • Architecture: ARMv8-A (aarch64)
  • OS: Raspberry Pi OS (Bookworm) or Debian 12+
  • Compiler: GCC 11+ (system default)

docs.title: Development Platforms
docs.text:
• Apple Silicon Macs: M1/M2/M3 chips (aarch64)
  • AWS Graviton: ARM64 cloud instances
  • Cross-compilation: x86_64 → ARM64

docs.title: Minimum Hardware
docs.text:
• RAM: 2GB minimum, 4GB recommended
  • Storage: 5GB free space for build artifacts
  • Network: Internet connection for dependency downloads

docs.title: Required System Packages
docs.text:
# Ubuntu/Debian/Raspberry Pi OS
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    ninja-build \
    python3 \
    python3-pip \
    git \
    pkg-config \
    libgpiod-dev \
    libmosquitto-dev \
    libcurl4-openssl-dev \
    libssl-dev \
    zlib1g-dev

docs.title: Conan Package Manager
docs.text:
# Install Conan
pip3 install conan

# Configure for ARM64
conan profile detect --force
conan remote add sparesparrow-conan \
    https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/sparesparrow-conan/openssl-conan/conan/

docs.title: Native ARM64 Profile (profiles/linux-arm64)
docs.text:
[settings]
os=Linux
arch=armv8
compiler=gcc
compiler.version=11
compiler.libcxx=libstdc++11
compiler.cppstd=17
build_type=Release

[options]
libgpiod/*:shared=False
jsoncpp/*:shared=False
mosquitto/*:shared=False
libcurl/*:shared=False
openssl/*:shared=False

[conf]
tools.cmake.cmaketoolchain:generator=Ninja
tools.cmake.cmaketoolchain:system_processor=aarch64
tools.system.package_manager:mode=install
tools.system.package_manager:sudo=True

docs.title: Cross-Compilation Profile (profiles/linux-x86_64)
docs.text:
For building ARM64 binaries on x86_64 hosts:

[settings]
os=Linux
arch=x86_64
compiler=gcc
compiler.version=13
compiler.libcxx=libstdc++11
compiler.cppstd=17
build_type=Release

[conf]
tools.cmake.cmaketoolchain:generator=Unix Makefiles

docs.title: Native ARM64 Build (Raspberry Pi)
docs.text:
1. Clone and setup: 

    git clone https://github.com/sparesparrow/mia.git
cd mia

  2. Install dependencies: 

    ./tools/install-deps-rpi.sh
./tools/bootstrap.sh

  3. Configure build: 

    cd apps/rpi-backend/cpp-audio  # platforms/cpp was removed; Conan flow tracked as P0-ARM64-1
conan install ../.. -pr:h=../../profiles/linux-arm64 -pr:b=../../profiles/linux-arm64 --build=missing

  4. Build: 

    mkdir -p build && cd build
cmake .. -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=../conan_toolchain.cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DWITH_HARDWARE=ON
make -j$(nproc)

docs.title: Cross-Compilation (x86_64 → ARM64)
docs.text:
1. Setup cross-compilation environment: 

    # Install ARM64 toolchain (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt install gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu g++-aarch64-linux-gnu

  2. Configure Conan: 

    cd apps/rpi-backend/cpp-audio  # platforms/cpp was removed; Conan flow tracked as P0-ARM64-1
conan install ../.. -pr:h=../../profiles/linux-arm64 -pr:b=../../profiles/linux-x86_64 --build=missing

  3. Cross-compile: 

    mkdir -p build && cd build
cmake .. -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=../conan_toolchain.cmake \
         -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
         -DWITH_HARDWARE=ON \
         -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=aarch64
make -j$(nproc)

docs.title: Automated Build Script
docs.text:
Use the provided build script for simplified builds:

# Native ARM64 build
./tools/build.sh --profile linux-arm64

# Cross-compilation
./tools/build.sh --profile linux-arm64 --cross-compile

# Clean rebuild
./tools/build.sh --clean --profile linux-arm64

docs.title: GPIO Library Compatibility
docs.text:
The project uses libgpiod v2.x API for GPIO control:

  • API Changes: v2.x simplified the API compared to v1.x
  • Direct Line Access: Uses gpiod_chip_get_line() and gpiod_line_request_*() functions
  • No Complex Configs: Eliminated settings/config structs for simpler code

docs.title: Compiler Optimizations
docs.text: ARM64-specific compiler flags: - -mcpu=cortex-a72: Raspberry Pi 4 optimization - -mcpu=cortex-a76: Raspberry Pi 5 optimization - -fPIC: Required for shared libraries - -O2: Recommended optimization level

docs.title: Memory Considerations
docs.text: ARM64 builds may require: - Swap space: Add 2GB swap for low-memory devices - Reduced parallelism: Use make -j2 instead of -j$(nproc) - Linker optimization: Use gold linker for faster linking

docs.title: 1. "relocation R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21 cannot be used when making a shared object"
docs.text: Cause: Static library compiled without -fPIC Fix: Ensure POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE TRUE in CMakeLists.txt

docs.title: 2. "libgpiod function not declared in scope"
docs.text: Cause: Using v1.x API with v2.x library Fix: Update code to use v2.x API (see HardwareControlServer.cpp changes)

docs.title: 3. "ARM aarch64 architecture not detected"
docs.text: Cause: Running on x86_64 emulation Fix: Ensure native ARM64 environment (check with uname -m)

docs.title: 4. Out of Memory Errors
docs.text:
Fix: 

# Add swap space
sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile

# Build with reduced parallelism
make -j2

docs.title: Verification Commands
docs.text:
Verify ARM64 build correctness:

# Check architecture
file hardware-server
# Should show: "ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64"

# Verify library dependencies
ldd hardware-server
# Should show ARM64 libraries

# Test basic functionality
./hardware-server --help

docs.title: GitHub Actions ARM64 Builds
docs.text: The project includes ARM64 CI builds using: - Native ARM64 runners: ubuntu-20.04-arm (if available) - Emulated ARM64: QEMU-based cross-compilation - Architecture validation: Automatic binary architecture checks

strategy:

    include:
      - { runner: ubuntu-latest, arch: x86_64, host_profile: linux-x86_64, build_profile: linux-x86_64 }
      - { runner: ubuntu-20.04, arch: arm64, host_profile: linux-arm64, build_profile: linux-arm64 }
      - { runner: ubuntu-latest, arch: arm64-cross, host_profile: linux-arm64, build_profile: linux-x86_64 }

docs.title: ARM64-Specific Optimizations
docs.text:
1. NEON Instructions: Vector processing for data-intensive operations
  2. Cache Alignment: 64-byte cache lines on ARM64
  3. Branch Prediction: Optimize conditional code patterns
  4. Memory Access: Use aligned memory access patterns

docs.title: Benchmarking
docs.text:
Monitor ARM64 performance:

# Build time measurement
time ./tools/build.sh --profile linux-arm64

# Runtime performance
perf stat ./hardware-server --benchmark

docs.title: From x86_64 Development
docs.text:
1. Update profiles: Switch from linux-release to linux-arm64
  2. Cross-compile first: Test builds before native ARM64 deployment
  3. Validate binaries: Always check file output for ARM64 architecture
  4. Test on target: Deploy and test on actual Raspberry Pi hardware

docs.title: API Compatibility
docs.text:
• FlatBuffers: Architecture-independent serialization
  • ZeroMQ: Cross-platform messaging
  • MQTT: Protocol-level compatibility
  • HTTP APIs: RESTful design works across architectures

docs.title: MIA Automotive Integration - Quick Start Guide
docs.text: Audience: End users, vehicle integrators, mechanics

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
MIA Automotive Integration enables real-time vehicle diagnostics through Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) communication between your Android device and a Raspberry Pi-based OBD-II adapter.

Primary prototype vehicle: Audi A4 Cabriolet 8H (2004)

docs.title: System Components
docs.text:
• Raspberry Pi: Acts as BLE OBD-II adapter, connects to vehicle's OBD-II port
  • Android App: Connects to Raspberry Pi via BLE, displays real-time vehicle data
  • OBD-II Protocol: Standard automotive diagnostic protocol

docs.title: 1. Install MIA App
docs.text:
1. Download MIA app from Google Play Store (or install APK from GitHub Releases)
  2. Open the app and grant Bluetooth permissions when prompted
  3. Navigate to the OBD screen

docs.title: 2. Power On Raspberry Pi
docs.text:
The Raspberry Pi should automatically start BLE services on boot:

# On Raspberry Pi, verify services are running
sudo systemctl status mia-ble-obd
sudo systemctl status mia-ble-advertiser

If services are not running, start them:

sudo systemctl start mia-ble-obd
sudo systemctl start mia-ble-advertiser

docs.title: 3. Connect Android App
docs.text:
1. Open MIA app on Android device
  2. Navigate to OBD screen
  3. Tap "Scan" button
  4. Wait for "MIA OBD-II Adapter" to appear in the device list
  5. Tap on "MIA OBD-II Adapter" to connect
  6. Wait for connection to establish (status will show "Connected")

docs.title: 4. View Real-Time Vehicle Data
docs.text: Once connected, the app will automatically start monitoring: - Engine RPM: Current engine revolutions per minute - Vehicle Speed: Current speed in km/h - Coolant Temperature: Engine coolant temperature in °C - Fuel Level: Current fuel level percentage - Engine Load: Current engine load percentage

docs.title: Supported Vehicles
docs.text:
• Audi A4 Cabriolet 8H (2004): Primary prototype — full VAG read-only diagnostics
  • Generic OBD-II: Any vehicle with ELM327-compatible OBD-II adapter
  • Citroën C4 (PSA): Legacy support via dedicated bridge module
  • Protocols: ISO 15765-4 (CAN), ISO 14230-4 (KWP2000), ISO 9141-2

docs.title: No Devices Found During Scan
docs.text:
Problem: Android app cannot find "MIA OBD-II Adapter"

Solutions: 1. Verify Raspberry Pi is powered on and in Bluetooth range (within 10 meters) 2. Check that BLE services are running: 

sudo systemctl status mia-ble-advertiser
3. Verify Bluetooth adapter is enabled: 
hciconfig hci0
# Should show "UP RUNNING"
4. Make Bluetooth discoverable: 
sudo hciconfig hci0 piscan

docs.title: Connection Fails
docs.text:
Problem: Android app cannot connect to Raspberry Pi

Solutions: 1. Check Bluetooth permissions in Android app settings 2. Verify BLE OBD service is running: 

sudo systemctl status mia-ble-obd
3. Check service logs for errors: 
sudo journalctl -u mia-ble-obd -n 50
4. Restart BLE services: 
sudo systemctl restart mia-ble-obd
sudo systemctl restart mia-ble-advertiser

docs.title: No Data Received
docs.text:
Problem: Connected but no OBD data is displayed

Solutions: 1. Verify OBD-II adapter is connected to vehicle's OBD-II port 2. Check that vehicle ignition is ON (engine may need to be running) 3. Verify OBD worker is running: 

sudo systemctl status mia-obd-worker
4. Check ZeroMQ broker is running: 
sudo systemctl status zmq-broker
5. Review logs: 
sudo journalctl -u mia-obd-worker -f

docs.title: OBD Simulator Automation & CI/CD Integration
docs.text: This document describes the automated dependency management, testing, and deployment processes for the MIA OBD Simulator components.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The OBD Simulator is now available as a canonical Conan package (sparetools-obd-sim/2.0.0) from the sparesparrow-conan remote. This package provides all necessary components for OBD simulation and replaces manual setup procedures.

The OBD Simulator has been integrated into the MIA automated build, test, and deployment pipeline using:

  • Conan for dependency management (via sparetools-obd-sim package)
  • pytest for unit and integration testing
  • GitHub Actions for CI/CD automation
  • Systemd for production deployment

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
1. Serial Bridge (rpi/hardware/serial_bridge.py)
  2. Reads ESP32/Arduino telemetry via USB Serial

  3. Publishes to ZeroMQ PUB socket (port 5556)

  4. OBD Worker (rpi/services/obd_worker.py)

  5. Subscribes to hardware telemetry
  6. Runs ELM327 emulator with dynamic PID responses

  7. Integrates with ZeroMQ broker (port 5555)

  8. Conan Recipe (rpi/conanfile.py)

  9. Manages Python service packaging
  10. Validates component dependencies

docs.title: Conan Integration
docs.text:
The OBD simulator is available as a pre-built Conan package:

# Install sparetools-obd-sim package (recommended)
conan install sparetools-obd-sim/2.0.0@ --build=missing

# Or build from source (legacy)
cd rpi
conan create . --build=missing

docs.title: SpareTools OBD-Sim Package
docs.text:
The canonical way to install OBD simulation capabilities is through the sparetools-obd-sim package:

# Add sparesparrow remote (if not already added)
conan remote add sparesparrow-conan https://sparesparrow.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/conan/sparesparrow-conan

# Install OBD simulator
conan install sparetools-obd-sim/2.0.0@ --build=missing

# Use bootstrap script from package
python -m sparetools_obd bootstrap

The package includes: - Pre-configured serial bridge and OBD worker services - Bootstrap scripts for automated setup - All required Python dependencies - Systemd service files

docs.title: Python Dependencies
docs.text:
Python dependencies are managed via rpi/requirements.txt:

fastapi>=0.104.0
uvicorn[standard]>=0.24.0
pydantic>=2.0.0
pyzmq>=25.1.0
psutil>=5.9.0
pyserial>=3.5
ELM327-emulator>=1.1.1

docs.title: System Dependencies
docs.text:
Required system packages (installed via apt-get):

sudo apt-get install -y \
    libzmq3-dev \
    python3-dev \
    python3-pip

docs.title: Unit Tests
docs.text:
Unit tests are located in tests/integration/test_obd_simulator.py:

# Run OBD simulator tests
python -m pytest tests/integration/test_obd_simulator.py -v

Test coverage includes: - Dynamic car state management - Serial bridge functionality - OBD worker initialization - ZeroMQ integration - PID encoding/decoding

docs.title: Integration Test Script
docs.text:
Automated integration test script:

# Run integration tests
bash tools/scripts/test-obd-simulator.sh

The script validates: - Component file presence - Python dependency availability - ZeroMQ communication - Mock mode operation

docs.title: 1. Main CI Pipeline (.github/workflows/main.yml)
docs.text: The main pipeline includes: - Python Tests: Runs OBD simulator tests as part of Python test suite - System Dependencies: Installs libzmq3-dev and python3-dev

docs.title: 2. RPi Python Services CI (.github/workflows/rpi-python-services.yml)
docs.text: Dedicated workflow for RPi Python services: - Multi-Python Testing: Tests on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 - Conan Build: Builds and validates Conan package - Deployment Validation: Validates deployment scripts and service files

docs.title: 3. Conan Build (ci/github-actions/rpi-python-conan.yml)
docs.text: Conan-specific workflow: - Builds Conan package for multiple Python versions - Validates package contents - Caches Conan dependencies

docs.title: Workflow Triggers
docs.text: Workflows trigger on: - Push to main, develop, or feature/* branches - Changes to rpi/** files - Pull requests affecting RPi components - Manual workflow dispatch

docs.title: Automated Deployment Script
docs.text:
The deployment script (tools/scripts/deploy-raspberry-pi.sh) has been updated to include:

  1. OBD Service Installation:
  2. Copies mia-serial-bridge.service
  3. Copies mia-obd-worker.service

  4. Installs Python dependencies from rpi/requirements.txt

  5. Service Management:

  6. Enables services to start on boot
  7. Provides status and log commands

docs.title: Using SpareTools Package (Recommended)
docs.text:
# Install sparetools-obd-sim package
conan install sparetools-obd-sim/2.0.0@ --build=missing

# Run bootstrap script from package
python -m sparetools_obd bootstrap

# Services will be automatically configured and started

docs.text:

sudo ./tools/scripts/deploy-raspberry-pi.sh

# Start services
sudo systemctl start zmq-broker
sudo systemctl start mia-serial-bridge
sudo systemctl start mia-obd-worker

# Check status
sudo systemctl status mia-obd-worker
sudo journalctl -u mia-obd-worker -f

docs.title: Pre-Deployment
docs.text:
• [ ] All tests pass in CI/CD pipeline
  • [ ] sparetools-obd-sim/2.0.0 package installs successfully
  • [ ] Conan package builds successfully (legacy)
  • [ ] Python dependencies install correctly via sparetools package
  • [ ] Service files reference correct paths
  • [ ] ZeroMQ ports are available (5555, 5556)

docs.title: Post-Deployment
docs.text:
• [ ] Services start without errors
  • [ ] Serial bridge detects hardware (or runs in mock mode)
  • [ ] OBD worker connects to broker
  • [ ] Telemetry flow works end-to-end
  • [ ] Logs show no critical errors

docs.title: CI/CD Failures
docs.text:
Issue: Tests fail due to missing dependencies - Solution: Ensure rpi/requirements.txt includes all required packages - Check: CI logs for specific missing package

Issue: Conan build fails - Solution: Verify rpi/conanfile.py syntax - Check: Conan cache is properly configured

Issue: sparetools-obd-sim package installation fails - Solution: Ensure sparesparrow-conan remote is added: conan remote add sparesparrow-conan https://sparesparrow.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/conan/sparesparrow-conan - Check: Conan version compatibility (requires Conan 2.0+)

docs.title: Deployment Issues
docs.text:
Issue: Services fail to start - Check: sudo journalctl -u mia-obd-worker -n 50 - Verify: Python dependencies installed: pip3 list | grep -E "pyzmq|pyserial|ELM327"

Issue: Serial bridge can't connect - Check: Serial port permissions: ls -l /dev/ttyUSB* - Solution: Add user to dialout group: sudo usermod -a -G dialout $USER

docs.title: Production Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide covers deploying the complete MIA vehicle telemetry and IoT system to a production Raspberry Pi.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Raspberry Pi 4B (recommended) or Pi 3B+
  • Raspberry Pi OS (Bullseye or later)
  • Internet connection for initial setup
  • OBD-II adapter (connected to vehicle's OBD-II port)
  • Root/sudo access

docs.title: Automated Deployment
docs.text:
The fastest way to deploy everything:

# On Raspberry Pi
cd /opt/mia
git pull origin main
sudo ./tools/scripts/deploy-production-rpi.sh

This script will: 1. Update code from repository 2. Set up BLE services 3. Deploy main services 4. Enable and start all services 5. Verify deployment

docs.title: Manual Deployment Steps
docs.text: If you prefer manual control:

docs.title: 1. Update Code
docs.text:
cd /opt/mia
git checkout main
git pull origin main

docs.title: 2. Setup BLE Services
docs.text: sudo ./tools/scripts/setup-ble-service.sh

docs.title: 3. Deploy Main Services
docs.text: sudo ./tools/scripts/deploy-raspberry-pi.sh

docs.title: 4. Enable Services
docs.text:
# Core services
sudo systemctl enable zmq-broker
sudo systemctl enable mia-api
sudo systemctl enable mia-gpio-worker

# OBD services
sudo systemctl enable mia-serial-bridge
sudo systemctl enable mia-obd-worker

# BLE services
sudo systemctl enable mia-ble-obd
sudo systemctl enable mia-ble-advertiser

docs.title: 5. Start Services
docs.text:
# Start in order (broker first)
sudo systemctl start zmq-broker
sleep 2

# Start core services
sudo systemctl start mia-api
sudo systemctl start mia-gpio-worker
sleep 2

# Start OBD services
sudo systemctl start mia-serial-bridge
sudo systemctl start mia-obd-worker
sleep 2

# Start BLE services
sudo systemctl start mia-ble-advertiser
sudo systemctl start mia-ble-obd

docs.title: Check Service Status

sudo systemctl status zmq-broker
sudo systemctl status mia-api
sudo systemctl status mia-gpio-worker
sudo systemctl status mia-serial-bridge
sudo systemctl status mia-obd-worker
sudo systemctl status mia-ble-obd
sudo systemctl status mia-ble-advertiser

sudo journalctl -u mia-ble-obd -f
sudo journalctl -u mia-ble-advertiser -f
sudo journalctl -u mia-obd-worker -f

# View all MIA service logs
sudo journalctl -u mia-* -f

docs.title: Test API Endpoints

curl http://localhost:8000/status

# List devices
curl http://localhost:8000/devices

# Get telemetry
curl http://localhost:8000/telemetry

hciconfig hci0

# Should show:

#         BD Address: XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX  ACL MTU: 1021:8  SCO MTU: 64:1
#         UP RUNNING PSCAN ISCAN

docs.text:
Edit /opt/mia/apps/rpi-backend/py-api/services/ble_advertiser.py:

DEVICE_NAME = "Your Custom Name"

Then restart: 

sudo systemctl restart mia-ble-advertiser

self.telemetry_interval = 0.1  # 10Hz (100ms)

Then restart:

docs.title: Service Health Checks
docs.text:
Create a health check script:

#!/bin/bash
# /opt/mia/tools/scripts/health-check.sh

services=(
    "zmq-broker"
    "mia-api"
    "mia-gpio-worker"
    "mia-serial-bridge"
    "mia-obd-worker"
    "mia-ble-obd"
    "mia-ble-advertiser"
)

for service in "${services[@]}"; do
    if systemctl is-active --quiet "$service"; then
        echo "✓ $service is running"
    else
        echo "✗ $service is not running"
        systemctl restart "$service"
    fi
done

Run as cron job: 

# Add to crontab
*/5 * * * * /opt/mia/tools/scripts/health-check.sh >> /var/log/mia/health-check.log 2>&1

docs.title: Services Won't Start
docs.text:
1. Check logs: 

    sudo journalctl -u <service-name> -n 50

  2. Check dependencies: 

    # Verify ZeroMQ broker is running
sudo systemctl status zmq-broker

# Verify Bluetooth is enabled
sudo systemctl status bluetooth

  3. Check permissions: 

    # Verify user has correct groups
groups mia
# Should include: bluetooth dialout gpio

docs.title: Bluetooth Issues
docs.text:
1. Reset Bluetooth adapter: 

    sudo hciconfig hci0 down
sudo hciconfig hci0 up

  2. Restart Bluetooth service: 

    sudo systemctl restart bluetooth

  3. Make discoverable: 

    sudo hciconfig hci0 piscan

docs.title: OBD Connection Issues
docs.text:
1. Verify OBD-II adapter is connected: 

    ls -l /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM*

  2. Check serial bridge logs: 

    sudo journalctl -u mia-serial-bridge -f

  3. Test OBD worker directly: 

    sudo -u mia python3 /opt/mia/apps/rpi-backend/py-api/services/obd_worker.py

docs.title: Backup Configuration
docs.text:
# Backup service files
sudo tar -czf /home/mia/backup-services-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz \
    /etc/systemd/system/mia-*.service \
    /opt/mia/apps/rpi-backend

docs.title: Restore from Backup
docs.text:
# Extract backup
sudo tar -xzf backup-services-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz -C /

# Reload systemd
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

# Restart services
sudo systemctl restart mia-*

docs.title: Update System
docs.text:
# Pull latest code
cd /opt/mia
git pull origin main

# Run deployment script
sudo ./tools/scripts/deploy-production-rpi.sh

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
# Checkout previous version
cd /opt/mia
git log --oneline
git checkout <previous-commit-hash>

# Redeploy
sudo ./tools/scripts/deploy-production-rpi.sh

docs.title: Change Default Passwords
docs.text:
# Change user password
sudo passwd mia

docs.title: Enable SSH Key Authentication
docs.text:
# Disable password authentication
sudo nano /etc/ssh/sshd_config
# Set: PasswordAuthentication no

sudo systemctl restart sshd

docs.title: Regular Updates
docs.text:
# Update system packages
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

# Update Python packages
sudo pip3 install --upgrade -r /opt/mia/requirements.txt

docs.title: Reduce Log Verbosity
docs.text:
Edit service files to change log level: 

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)  # Instead of INFO

docs.title: Adjust Service Priorities
docs.text:
Edit systemd service files: 

[Service]
Nice=10  # Lower priority (higher number = lower priority)

docs.title: MIA Raspberry Pi Setup Guide
docs.text:
This guide covers setting up the MIA build environment on Raspberry Pi (and other Debian-based ARM systems) without requiring system-level pip installations.

The setup uses sparetools-cpython packages from Cloudsmith for zero-copy Python environment management via Conan.

docs.title: Quick Start (Recommended)
docs.text:
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/sparesparrow/mia.git
cd mia

# 2. Install system dependencies (requires sudo)
./tools/install-deps-rpi.sh

# 3. Bootstrap environment (downloads from Cloudsmith)
./tools/bootstrap.sh

# 4. Build
./tools/build.sh

docs.title: Alternative: Using init.sh
docs.text:
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/sparesparrow/mia.git
cd mia

# 2. Install system dependencies (requires sudo)
./tools/install-deps-rpi.sh

# 3. Initialize the environment (sets up everything)
./tools/init.sh

# 4. Activate and build
source tools/env.sh
mia-build

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: The setup requires: - Raspberry Pi 3/4/5 or compatible ARM64/ARMv7 device - Raspberry Pi OS (Bookworm or later) or Debian 12+ - At least 2GB RAM recommended for compilation - Internet connection for downloading dependencies

docs.title: Step 1: Install System Dependencies
docs.text:
Run the dependency installer:

./tools/install-deps-rpi.sh

This installs: - Build tools: cmake, ninja-build, g++ - Python: python3, python3-venv, python3-pip - Libraries: libgpiod-dev, libmosquitto-dev, libcurl4-openssl-dev, etc. - Runtime: mosquitto MQTT broker

For a minimal installation (build tools only):

./tools/install-deps-rpi.sh --minimal

docs.title: Step 2: Bootstrap Build Environment
docs.text:
The bootstrap script creates a self-contained Python environment with Conan, using the sparetools zero-copy approach:

./tools/bootstrap.sh

This: 1. Tries to install sparetools-cpython/3.12.7 from Conan (Cloudsmith remote) 2. Creates zero-copy symlinks from Conan cache to .buildenv/ 3. Falls back to system Python with venv if Conan CPython unavailable 4. Installs Conan, CMake, and other build tools 5. Configures Conan profiles for the project

The environment is isolated from system Python, avoiding PEP 668 issues.

docs.title: Cloudsmith Remote Integration
docs.text:
The project uses sparetools-cpython packages from Cloudsmith for zero-copy Python environments:

  • sparetools-cpython: Portable CPython 3.12.7 via Conan
  • Zero-copy symlinks: Saves disk space by linking to Conan cache
  • Cloudsmith remote: Pre-built packages available at: https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/sparesparrow-conan/openssl-conan/conan/

The bootstrap scripts automatically configure the Conan remote. To manually set it up:

conan remote add sparesparrow-conan \
    https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/sparesparrow-conan/openssl-conan/conan/

docs.title: Step 3: Activate Environment (Optional)
docs.text:
For interactive development:

source tools/env.sh

This provides: - Activated Python virtual environment - conan and cmake on PATH - Helper functions: mia-build, mia-clean, mia-info

docs.title: Step 4: Build
docs.text:
Build all components:

./tools/build.sh

Build specific components:

./tools/build.sh hardware-server
./tools/build.sh mcp-server

Clean and rebuild:

./tools/build.sh --clean

Use a specific Conan profile:

./tools/build.sh --profile linux-arm64

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
After setup:

mia/
├── .buildenv/              # Build environment (gitignored)
│   ├── venv/               # Python virtual environment
│   ├── conan/              # Conan home directory
│   ├── cache/              # Downloaded files cache
│   └── python/             # Standalone CPython (if used)
├── tools/
│   ├── bootstrap.sh        # Environment setup script
│   ├── build.sh            # Build wrapper
│   ├── env.sh              # Environment activation
│   └── install-deps-rpi.sh # System dependency installer
├── build-Release/          # Build output
└── ...

docs.title: "externally-managed-environment" Error
docs.text:
This error means you're trying to use pip install directly on system Python. Use the bootstrap script instead:

./tools/bootstrap.sh

docs.title: CMake Can't Find Libraries
docs.text:
Make sure system dependencies are installed:

./tools/install-deps-rpi.sh

Then rebuild:

./tools/build.sh --clean

docs.title: Conan Profile Issues
docs.text:
Reset Conan configuration:

source tools/env.sh
conan profile detect --force

docs.title: Out of Memory During Build
docs.text:
Reduce parallel jobs:

./tools/build.sh --jobs 1

Or add swap space:

sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile

docs.title: Updating the Build Environment
docs.text:
To update Conan and other tools:

./tools/bootstrap.sh --update

To completely reinstall:

./tools/bootstrap.sh --clean

docs.title: Cross-Compilation
docs.text:
To cross-compile for Raspberry Pi from x86_64:

  1. Install the ARM toolchain on your build machine
  2. Use the appropriate Conan profile:
./tools/build.sh --profile linux-arm64

docs.title: Available Conan Profiles
docs.text: Profile Description linux-arm64 Raspberry Pi 4/5 (64-bit) linux-release x86_64 Linux linux-simulation For testing without hardware

docs.title: Built Components
docs.text:
After a successful build:

Component Description Port hardware-server GPIO control server 8081 mcp-server MCP tools server 8082 webgrab-client Download client - webgrab-server Download server 8083

docs.title: Running the Services
docs.text:
Start the hardware server:

./build-Release/hardware-server

Start with custom configuration:

./build-Release/hardware-server --port 8081 --config config.json

docs.title: Integration with Python Modules
docs.text:
The C++ hardware server communicates with Python modules via MQTT:

# Start MQTT broker
sudo systemctl start mosquitto

# Start hardware server
./build-Release/hardware-server &

# Run Python orchestrator
source tools/env.sh
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m modules.core-orchestrator

docs.title: API Authentication Setup
docs.text:
The MIA API service requires authentication for production use. Create the environment file:

# Create environment directory
sudo mkdir -p /etc/mia

# Generate API key (run as non-root user)
python3 -c "import secrets; print('MIA_API_KEY=mia_api_' + secrets.token_hex(16))" | sudo tee /etc/mia/environment

# Set proper permissions
sudo chmod 600 /etc/mia/environment
sudo chown root:root /etc/mia/environment

The API service will automatically load this key. For development, you can disable authentication by adding MIA_AUTH_DISABLED=1 to the environment file.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Main README
  • C++ Platform Documentation
  • API Reference
  • Architecture Overview

docs.title: Repository Switching Guide
docs.text: The AI-SERVIS bootstrap system supports easy switching between Cloudsmith and GitHub Packages for artifact downloads.

docs.title: Using Cloudsmith (Default)
docs.text:
# No configuration needed - Cloudsmith is the default
./tools/bootstrap.sh

docs.title: Using GitHub Packages
docs.text:
# Option 1: Use the helper script
source tools/repo-config.sh github
./tools/bootstrap.sh

# Option 2: Set environment variables manually
export ARTIFACT_REPO=github
export GITHUB_OWNER=sparesparrow
export GITHUB_REPO=cpy
export GITHUB_TAG=v3.12.7
./tools/bootstrap.sh

docs.title: Using GitHub Packages with Authentication
docs.text:
For private repositories or authenticated access:

# Using helper script
source tools/repo-config.sh github --token YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN
./tools/bootstrap.sh

# Or set environment variable
export ARTIFACT_REPO=github
export GITHUB_TOKEN=your_token_here
./tools/bootstrap.sh

docs.title: Cloudsmith Configuration
docs.text: Variable Default Description ARTIFACT_REPO cloudsmith Repository type: cloudsmith or github CLOUDSMITH_CPY_BASE https://dl.cloudsmith.io/sparesparrow/cpy/raw/versions Base URL for CPython tool downloads CLOUDSMITH_CONAN_REMOTE https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/sparesparrow-conan/openssl-conan/conan/ Conan remote URL

docs.title: GitHub Packages Configuration
docs.text: Variable Default Description ARTIFACT_REPO cloudsmith Set to github to use GitHub Packages GITHUB_OWNER sparesparrow GitHub organization or username GITHUB_REPO cpy Repository name GITHUB_TAG v3.12.7 Release tag (e.g., v3.12.7, latest) GITHUB_TOKEN (none) Personal access token for authenticated access GITHUB_USER sparesparrow GitHub username for Conan authentication GITHUB_CONAN_REMOTE https://maven.pkg.github.com/sparesparrow/conan Conan remote URL for GitHub Packages

docs.title: Cloudsmith
docs.text:
• CPython Tool: https://dl.cloudsmith.io/sparesparrow/cpy/raw/versions/{VERSION}/cpython-tool-{VERSION}-{PLATFORM}.tar.gz
  • Conan Remote: https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/sparesparrow-conan/openssl-conan/conan/

docs.title: GitHub Packages
docs.text:
• CPython Tool (Releases): https://github.com/{OWNER}/{REPO}/releases/download/{TAG}/cpython-tool-{VERSION}-{PLATFORM}.tar.gz
  • Conan Remote: https://maven.pkg.github.com/{OWNER}/conan

docs.title: Switch to GitHub Packages for a session
docs.text:
# Set configuration
source tools/repo-config.sh github

# Run bootstrap
./tools/bootstrap.sh

# Or use complete-bootstrap.py directly
python3 complete-bootstrap.py

docs.title: Use GitHub Packages with custom settings
docs.text:
export ARTIFACT_REPO=github
export GITHUB_OWNER=myorg
export GITHUB_REPO=my-cpy-repo
export GITHUB_TAG=v3.12.7
export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxx

python3 complete-bootstrap.py

docs.title: Switch back to Cloudsmith
docs.text:
source tools/repo-config.sh cloudsmith
# or
export ARTIFACT_REPO=cloudsmith
unset GITHUB_TOKEN GITHUB_OWNER GITHUB_REPO GITHUB_TAG

docs.title: Repository Helper Script
docs.text:
The tools/repo-config.sh script provides a convenient way to switch repositories:

# Use Cloudsmith (default)
source tools/repo-config.sh cloudsmith

# Use GitHub Packages (public)
source tools/repo-config.sh github

# Use GitHub Packages with authentication
source tools/repo-config.sh github --token ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxx

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
- name: Bootstrap with GitHub Packages
  env:
    ARTIFACT_REPO: github
    GITHUB_OWNER: sparesparrow
    GITHUB_REPO: cpy
    GITHUB_TAG: v3.12.7
    GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  run: python3 complete-bootstrap.py

docs.title: GitLab CI
docs.text:
bootstrap:
  variables:
    ARTIFACT_REPO: "github"
    GITHUB_OWNER: "sparesparrow"
    GITHUB_REPO: "cpy"
    GITHUB_TAG: "v3.12.7"
    GITHUB_TOKEN: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"
  script:
    - python3 complete-bootstrap.py

docs.title: GitHub Packages 404 Error
docs.text:
If you get a 404 error when using GitHub Packages:

  1. Verify the release tag exists: https://github.com/{OWNER}/{REPO}/releases/tag/{TAG}
  2. Check that the filename matches: cpython-tool-{VERSION}-{PLATFORM}.tar.gz
  3. Ensure the repository is public or you have access with your token

docs.title: GitHub Packages Authentication
docs.text:
For private repositories or authenticated access:

  1. Create a GitHub Personal Access Token with read:packages permission
  2. Set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  3. For Conan, also set GITHUB_USER (usually your GitHub username)

docs.title: Switching Between Repositories
docs.text:
The bootstrap script reads environment variables at runtime, so you can switch repositories by:

  1. Setting ARTIFACT_REPO environment variable
  2. Running the bootstrap script again (it will use the new configuration)
  3. No need to clean .buildenv/ unless you want a fresh download

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The bootstrap script uses only Python stdlib - no external dependencies
  • Repository switching is done via environment variables for maximum flexibility
  • Both Cloudsmith and GitHub Packages use the same CPython tool tarball format
  • Conan remotes are automatically configured based on the selected repository
  • GitHub Packages authentication is optional for public repositories

docs.title: Automated LineageOS 14.1 + Magisk Root Installation for HTC One M7 Development
docs.text: This guide provides step-by-step instructions for setting up HTC One M7 devices with LineageOS 14.1 and Magisk root access, specifically configured for MIA automotive application development.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Prerequisites
  2. Environment Setup
  3. Device Preparation
  4. Automated Installation
  5. Post-Installation Configuration
  6. Verification and Testing
  7. Backup and Recovery
  8. Troubleshooting
  9. Maintenance

docs.title: Hardware Requirements
docs.text:
• HTC One M7 device (unlocked bootloader required)
  • USB cable (for device connection)
  • Ubuntu 24.04 LTS host system (recommended)
  • Minimum 10GB free disk space

docs.title: Software Requirements
docs.text:
• Bash shell environment
  • ADB and Fastboot tools
  • wget/curl for downloads
  • unzip for archive extraction

docs.title: Device Requirements
docs.text:
• Unlocked bootloader (required for custom ROM installation)
  • USB debugging enabled
  • Device authorized for USB debugging
  • Battery charged above 50%

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
⚠️ IMPORTANT WARNINGS:

  • This process will wipe all data on your HTC One M7
  • Unlocking the bootloader may void your warranty
  • Root access can compromise device security
  • Custom ROMs may have stability issues

Backup all important data before proceeding!

docs.title: 1. Verify Host Environment
docs.text:
Run the environment verification script to ensure your Ubuntu system is properly configured:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/environment
./verify-environment.sh

This script will: - Check Ubuntu 24.04 compatibility - Install required packages (adb, fastboot, wget, curl, unzip) - Verify Android tools versions - Setup udev rules for device access - Create working directory structure

docs.title: 2. Grant USB Access
docs.text:
After running the environment script, add your user to the plugdev group and reboot:

sudo usermod -aG plugdev $USER
# Log out and back in, or reboot

docs.title: 1. Unlock Bootloader
docs.text:
⚠️ This will wipe all data on your device!

  1. Power off your HTC One M7
  2. Boot into bootloader mode:
  3. Hold Volume Down + Power buttons simultaneously
  4. Use Volume keys to select "FASTBOOT"

  5. Press Power to confirm

  6. Connect device to computer via USB

  7. Verify fastboot connection: 

    fastboot devices

  8. Unlock bootloader (this erases all data): 

    fastboot oem unlock

  9. Follow on-screen instructions on device

docs.title: 2. Verify Device Connection
docs.text:
Run the device verification script:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/environment
./device-manager.sh setup

This will: - Detect your HTC One M7 - Verify bootloader status - Confirm HTC One M7 compatibility - Test USB connection stability

docs.title: Option 1: Full Automated Installation (Recommended)
docs.text:
Run the master installation script:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/installation
./install-lineageos.sh

The script will automatically: 1. Verify environment and device 2. Download LineageOS 14.1 and GApps 3. Install TWRP recovery 4. Wipe device partitions 5. Flash LineageOS ROM and GApps 6. Install Magisk for root access 7. Configure device for development 8. Setup MIA application environment

docs.title: Option 2: Manual Step-by-Step Installation
docs.text: If you prefer more control, run individual phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Recovery Installation
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/recovery
./twrp-manager.sh install
./verify-recovery.sh verify

docs.title: Phase 2: Download Files
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/rom
./rom-manager.sh download-all

docs.title: Phase 3: Transfer Files to Device
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/rom
./file-transfer.sh batch <device_serial> <rom_file> <gapps_file>

docs.title: Phase 4: Flash ROM
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/installation
./flash-operations.sh wipe <device_serial>
./flash-operations.sh flash-rom <device_serial>
./flash-operations.sh flash-gapps <device_serial>

docs.title: Phase 5: Install Root
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/root
./magisk-manager.sh install <device_serial>

docs.title: Phase 6: Post-Installation Setup
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/post-install
./setup-dev-environment.sh configure <device_serial>
./mia-integration.sh setup <device_serial>

docs.title: Post-Installation Configuration
docs.text:
After installation completes, the device will reboot into LineageOS 14.1. Complete the initial Android setup:

  1. Language Selection: Choose your preferred language
  2. WiFi Setup: Connect to a WiFi network
  3. Google Account: Skip or add Google account (optional)
  4. Device Setup: Complete basic device configuration
  5. Developer Options: Will be automatically enabled

docs.title: 1. Health Check
docs.text:
Run a comprehensive health check:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/testing
./health-check.sh full <device_serial>

This verifies: - Boot stability - Core functionality (WiFi, Bluetooth, GPS) - Battery health - Performance metrics - Hardware sensors

docs.title: 2. MIA Test Suite
docs.text:
Run MIA-specific tests:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/testing
./test-suite.sh full <device_serial>

This tests: - MIA app installation - Root access verification - BLE connectivity - OBD interface access - MQTT networking - Performance benchmarks

docs.title: 3. Root Verification
docs.text:
Verify root access:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/root
./verify-root.sh verify <device_serial>

docs.title: Creating Backups
docs.text:
Always create backups before making changes:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/backup
./backup-manager.sh create full <device_serial>

docs.title: Types of Backups
docs.text:
• System Backup: Complete system image
  • Data Backup: User data and applications
  • Boot Backup: Boot partition only

docs.title: Recovery Procedures
docs.text: If something goes wrong:

docs.title: Boot Loop Recovery
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/backup
./recovery-procedures.sh bootloop <device_serial>

docs.title: Failed Installation Rollback
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/backup
./recovery-procedures.sh rollback <device_serial>

docs.title: Emergency Recovery
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/backup
./recovery-procedures.sh bricked <device_serial>

docs.title: Device Not Detected
docs.text:
# Check USB connection
lsusb | grep HTC

# Restart ADB server
adb kill-server
adb start-server

# Check device authorization
adb devices

docs.title: Fastboot Not Working
docs.text:
# Verify fastboot installation
fastboot --version

# Check device in fastboot mode
fastboot devices

docs.title: Installation Fails
docs.text:
# Check logs
tail -f android-device-workspace/logs/installation.log

# Run diagnostics
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/backup
./recovery-procedures.sh diagnostics <device_serial>

docs.title: Root Not Working
docs.text:
# Verify Magisk installation
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/root
./verify-root.sh verify <device_serial>

# Reinstall Magisk
./magisk-manager.sh install <device_serial>

docs.title: Log Files
docs.text: All operations are logged to: - android-device-workspace/logs/ - Main operation logs - android-device-workspace/test-results/ - Test results - android-device-workspace/reports/ - Generated reports

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
1. Check the logs in android-device-workspace/logs/
  2. Run diagnostics using recovery procedures
  3. Generate reports for detailed analysis
  4. Check device forums for HTC One M7 specific issues

docs.title: Weekly Health Checks
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/testing
./health-check.sh full <device_serial>

docs.title: Monthly Backups
docs.text:
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/backup
./backup-manager.sh create full <device_serial>

docs.title: Update Management
docs.text:
# Update Magisk
cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/root
./magisk-manager.sh update <device_serial>

# Update MIA app (when available)
# Deploy updated APK through development workflow

docs.title: Performance Monitoring
docs.text:
Monitor device performance:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/testing
./health-check.sh performance <device_serial>

docs.title: Storage Management
docs.text:
Clean up old backups:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/backup
./backup-manager.sh clean <device_serial>

docs.title: Custom Configuration
docs.text: Edit configuration files in android-device-workspace/: - installation-config.txt - Installation settings - installation-checkpoint.txt - Resume interrupted installations

docs.title: Manual Operations
docs.text:
All automated scripts can be run individually for manual control:

# Environment
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/environment/verify-environment.sh
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/environment/device-manager.sh setup

# Recovery
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/recovery/twrp-manager.sh install
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/recovery/verify-recovery.sh verify

# Downloads
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/rom/rom-manager.sh download-all

# Installation
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/installation/flash-operations.sh wipe
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/installation/flash-operations.sh flash-rom

# Root
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/root/magisk-manager.sh install

# Configuration
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/post-install/setup-dev-environment.sh configure
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/post-install/mia-integration.sh setup

# Testing
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/testing/health-check.sh full
./tools/scripts/android-device-setup/testing/test-suite.sh full

docs.title: Report Generation
docs.text:
Generate comprehensive reports:

cd tools/scripts/android-device-setup/reporting
./generate-report.sh comprehensive <device_serial>

Available report types: - installation - Installation progress and status - system - Device system information - performance - Performance metrics and benchmarks - health - Health assessment and diagnostics - backup - Backup status and history - testing - Test results and analysis - comprehensive - Complete system analysis

docs.text:
• LineageOS Wiki: https://wiki.lineageos.org/devices/m7
  • TWRP Documentation: https://twrp.me/Devices/HTCOneM7.html
  • Magisk Documentation: https://topjohnwu.github.io/Magisk/
  • Android Developer Tools: https://developer.android.com/studio/run/device

docs.title: AI-Servis CI/CD & Development Environment
docs.text: This document describes the comprehensive CI/CD pipeline and development environment setup for the AI-Servis project.

docs.title: Development Environment
docs.text:
# Start development environment
./tools/scripts/dev-environment.sh up dev

# Start with monitoring
./tools/scripts/dev-environment.sh up full

# Check status
./tools/scripts/dev-environment.sh status dev

# View logs
./tools/scripts/dev-environment.sh logs dev --follow

docs.title: VS Code Development Container
docs.text:
1. Install the "Dev Containers" extension
  2. Open the project in VS Code
  3. Press Ctrl+Shift+P and select "Dev Containers: Reopen in Container"
  4. Wait for the container to build and start

docs.title: Main CI/CD Pipeline (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
docs.text:
Triggers: - Push to main or develop branches - Pull requests to main - Path-scoped: only runs when Python, C++, ESP32, schema, or CI-owned files change

Jobs: 1. Detect Changes - Path-based change detection so the workflow only runs relevant platform jobs 2. Schema Validation - FlatBuffers compilation checks for schemas/ and webgrab.fbs 3. Lint - Python formatting and lint checks for maintained Python surfaces 4. Python Tests - pytest tests/ -m "not hardware" under the bundled CPython/Conan flow 5. Build C++ - Native build validation for the C++ surfaces when native paths change 6. Build ESP32 - PlatformIO build validation when apps/esp32 changes

docs.title: Conan Dependency Management Setup
docs.text: This document describes how to use Conan for dependency management in the ai-servis project.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Install Conan: 

    pip install conan

  2. Configure Conan (first time only): 

    conan profile detect --force

docs.title: Project Dependencies
docs.text:
The project uses the following dependencies managed by Conan:

  • libgpiod: GPIO control library for Raspberry Pi
  • jsoncpp: JSON parsing library
  • mosquitto: MQTT client for ESP32 communication
  • libcurl: HTTP client for LLM API calls

docs.title: Option 1: Using the Build Script
docs.text:
The easiest way is to use the provided build script:

./tools/scripts/build-hardware-server.sh

docs.title: Option 2: Manual Build
docs.text:
1. Install dependencies: 

    cd src/hardware/build
conan install ../../.. --profile ../../../profiles/linux-release --build missing

  2. Configure CMake: 

    cmake ../.. -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=conan_toolchain.cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

  3. Build: 

    make -j$(nproc)

...

os=Windows
arch=x86_64

docs.text:
• Canonical Compose files live in infra/docker/; use docker compose -f infra/docker/docker-compose.dev.yml config to validate the dev stack before starting it.
  • The root-level tests/env/docker-compose.pi-simulation.yml keeps only the runnable broker/state services enabled by default. Add --profile legacy-sim only if you also maintain the older simulator images.
  • If docker compose build fails while pulling base images with a gpg: public key decryption failed or Docker credential timeout, fix the local Docker credential helper first and retry the build.

docs.title: ZeroMQ Broker and Service Health
docs.text:
The ZeroMQ broker must be running before any dependent service starts. To verify:

# Check broker status
sudo systemctl status zmq-broker

# Check core service chain
sudo systemctl status zmq-broker mia-api mia-serial-bridge mia-obd-worker

# Verify broker is listening on port 5555
ss -tlnp | grep 5555

# Verify telemetry PUB/SUB on port 5556
ss -tlnp | grep 5556

# Quick API health check
curl -s http://localhost:8000/status

If the broker is not running, all dependent services will fail to connect. Restart in order:

sudo systemctl restart zmq-broker
sleep 2
sudo systemctl restart mia-api mia-gpio-worker mia-serial-bridge
sleep 2
sudo systemctl restart mia-obd-worker

docs.title: L1 – Basic Verification
docs.text:
• Power: Check PD/QC adapter, cables, and fuse
  • ESP32: Visible via BLE? RSSI should be > −80 dBm
  • OBD data: Arriving? Check fuel/RPM in dashboard
  • Camera: Image feed and ANPR enabled?

docs.title: L2 – Network and Messaging
docs.text:
• MQTT broker: Running? Check reconnect logs
  • Wi‑Fi Direct / SoftAP: Throughput verified
  • mDNS discovery: Android ↔ Pi resolution working

docs.title: L3 – Diagnostics and Logs
docs.text:
• Export application logs (BLE, ANPR, OBD services)
  • ESP32: serial line, bitrate/filters, watchdog
  • Pi gateway: RTSP ingest, disk space, health checks
# View all MIA service logs
sudo journalctl -u "mia-*" --since "1 hour ago"

# Follow a specific service
sudo journalctl -u mia-serial-bridge -f

# Check for errors across all services
sudo journalctl -u "mia-*" -p err --since "1 hour ago"

If the problem persists, open an issue with logs and device versions.

docs.title: 🖥️ AI-Servis VM Testing Guide
docs.text: This guide provides comprehensive instructions for testing the AI-Servis CI/CD infrastructure in virtual machine environments.

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text: The VM testing suite validates the complete AI-Servis development and deployment infrastructure in a clean, isolated environment. This ensures that the setup works correctly across different systems and configurations.

docs.text:
# In your VM, download the test script
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-servis/ai-servis/main/scripts/vm-test-setup.sh
chmod +x vm-test-setup.sh

# Or if you have the repository
git clone https://github.com/ai-servis/ai-servis.git
cd mia
./tools/scripts/vm-test-setup.sh

docs.title: 🧪 Test Phases
docs.text: The VM test suite runs through 8 comprehensive test phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: System Requirements ✅
docs.text:
Duration: ~2 minutes

  • Memory Check - Validates sufficient RAM (8GB+)
  • Disk Space Check - Validates free space (50GB+)
  • Command Availability - Checks for required tools
  • Network Connectivity - Tests internet access
# Manual validation:
free -h                    # Check memory
df -h                     # Check disk space
curl -s https://github.com # Test connectivity

docs.title: Phase 2: Docker Setup ✅
docs.text:
Duration: ~5 minutes

  • Docker Installation - Installs Docker if missing
  • Docker Daemon - Validates Docker is running
  • Docker Compose - Tests compose functionality
  • Docker Buildx - Tests multi-platform builds
# Manual validation:
docker --version
docker compose version
docker buildx version
docker info

docs.title: Phase 3: Project Setup ✅
docs.text:
Duration: ~3 minutes

  • Repository Clone - Downloads/copies project
  • Dependencies - Installs Python requirements
  • Pre-commit Hooks - Sets up code quality tools
  • Script Permissions - Makes scripts executable
# Manual validation:
ls -la tools/scripts/           # Check script permissions
pip3 list | grep pytest   # Check Python deps
pre-commit --version      # Check pre-commit

docs.title: Phase 4: Development Environment ✅
docs.text:
Duration: ~8 minutes

  • Environment Startup - Starts dev docker-compose
  • Service Health - Tests all service endpoints
  • Database Connectivity - PostgreSQL and Redis
  • MQTT Broker - Message broker functionality
# Manual validation:
./tools/scripts/dev-environment.sh status dev
curl http://localhost:8080/health
curl http://localhost:8090/health

docs.title: Phase 5: Pi Simulation ✅
docs.text:
Duration: ~6 minutes

  • Simulation Startup - Pi simulation environment
  • GPIO Simulator - Hardware simulation web UI
  • ESP32 Simulators - Device emulation
  • Hardware Monitor - Performance monitoring
# Manual validation:
./tools/scripts/dev-environment.sh status pi-sim
curl http://localhost:8084  # Pi Gateway
curl http://localhost:9000  # GPIO Simulator

docs.title: Phase 6: Monitoring Stack ✅
docs.text:
Duration: ~8 minutes

  • Prometheus - Metrics collection service
  • Grafana - Visualization dashboard
  • AlertManager - Alert routing system
  • Jaeger - Distributed tracing
  • Uptime Kuma - Service monitoring
# Manual validation:
./tools/scripts/dev-environment.sh status monitoring
open http://localhost:3000   # Grafana
open http://localhost:9090   # Prometheus

docs.title: Phase 7: CI Simulation ✅
docs.text:
Duration: ~5 minutes

  • Code Linting - Python code quality checks
  • Docker Builds - Container build testing
  • Multi-platform - Cross-platform build tools
  • Security Scanning - Basic vulnerability checks
# Manual validation:
flake8 --version
docker build --help
./tools/scripts/docker-build-multiplatform.sh --help

docs.title: Phase 8: Performance Validation ✅
docs.text:
Duration: ~3 minutes

  • Performance Tests - Load testing validation
  • Resource Usage - CPU and memory monitoring
  • Response Times - Service performance
  • System Health - Overall system status
# Manual validation:
./tools/scripts/performance-tests.sh
top                      # Check CPU usage
free -h                  # Check memory usage

docs.title: Wiring & Power (OBD‑II / CAN)
docs.text: Rychlá referenční karta pro připojení ESP32 na OBD-II. Podrobnosti, napájení v autě, vstupy/výstupy a revize firmwaru: Zapojení ESP32 modulů do MIA.

docs.title: 1. Konektor OBD-II — které piny potřebuješ
docs.text: Pin Signál Pozn. 6 CAN_H kroucený pár s pinem 14 14 CAN_L 4 / 5 Kostra / signálová zem použij jednu, ne obě 7 K‑line starší KWP2000 jednotky; MIA zatím nepoužívá 16 +12 V trvalých nenapájet odsud Raspberry Pi — tenký, slabě jištěný vodič pro diagnostiku

docs.title: 2. Volba budiče — SN65HVD230 ano, TJA1050 ne
docs.text: Dřívější verze tohoto dokumentu uváděla „SN65HVD230/TJA1050" jako zaměnitelné. Nejsou: TJA1050 je 5V budič a ESP32 není 5V tolerantní — jeho RXD by na 3,3V vstup pustil 5 V. Použij 3,3V typ (SN65HVD230, TJA1051T/3 s pinem VIO), nebo dej na RXD převodník úrovní.

docs.title: Zapojení SN65HVD230 → ESP32
docs.text:
Budič ESP32 VCC 3V3 ne 5 V GND GND společná zem RXD GPIO16 budič → ESP32 TXD GPIO17 ESP32 → budič; pro pasivní odposlech nezapojuj Rs 10 kΩ na GND normální rychlost CANH / CANL OBD 6 / 14 kroucený pár

Piny odpovídají zdrojáku apps/esp32/firmware-obd/components/ai_servis_obd/ai_servis_obd.c.

docs.title: 3. Napájení
docs.text:
graph LR
  OBD["Palubní síť 12 V<br/>KL.30 přes pojistku 1 A"]
  BUCK["Měnič 12 V → 5 V<br/>vstup 6–36 V, ≥ 1 A"]
  CAP["Bulk 220–470 µF<br/>u modulu"]
  ESP["ESP32 DevKit<br/>pin 5V/VIN"]
  TRX["SN65HVD230<br/>z 3V3 ESP32"]
  OBD --> BUCK --> CAP --> ESP --> TRX
  • Vstupní rozsah měniče 6–36 V: při startování motoru napětí padá hluboko pod 9 V.
  • Bulk kondenzátor u modulu pokryje vysílací špičky WiFi (~500 mA), jinak Brownout detector was triggered.
  • Společná zem: OBD GND → měnič → ESP32 → budič, všechno na jeden bod.
  • Nikdy nenapájej desku z USB a z auta současně — při flashování odpoj auto.

docs.title: 4. Parametry sběrnice
docs.text:
• Bitrate 500 kbit/s, 11bitové identifikátory (EU vozy zhruba po r. 2008).
  • Dotazy na 0x7DF, odpovědi z 0x7E8.

docs.title: Terminace: v autě ne, na stole ano
docs.text:
Kde 120 Ω Proč V autě na OBD nepřidávej sběrnice je zakončená z výroby na obou koncích Na stole (ESP32 ↔ ESP32 / USB-CAN) 2× 120 Ω bez nich se nedomluví nic

Moduly SN65HVD230 z tržiště mívají 120 Ω osazený napevno — před montáží do auta ho vypájej nebo přeřízni propojku.

docs.title: 5. Bezpečnost
docs.text:
• Pro odposlech používej listen-only: TWAI_MODE_LISTEN_ONLY a zároveň fyzicky nezapojený vodič TXD. Softwarový přepínač je registr, který chyba v kódu přepíše; nezapojený drát ne.
  • Pojistka 0,5–1 A co nejblíž odbočce, kroucený pár pro CAN, jediný zemnící bod.
  • Žluté konektory ve voze jsou airbagy — nesahat.

Odposlechová varianta firmwaru

ai_servis_obd.c se ve výchozím stavu instaluje v TWAI_MODE_NORMAL, protože posílá OBD dotazy. Pasivní sestavení: idf.py build -DMIA_TWAI_LISTEN_ONLY=1 — ovladač pak jede v TWAI_MODE_LISTEN_ONLY a ai_servis_obd_read_pid() nevysílá. Souvislosti a další opravy v téhle komponentě: nálezy proti firmwaru.

docs.title: MIA API Reference
docs.text:
The MIA API is a REST/WebSocket API for controlling IoT devices and receiving telemetry data.

Base URL: http://<rpi-address>:8000

Interactive Docs: http://<rpi-address>:8000/docs (Swagger UI)

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Authentication is optional but recommended for production deployments.

docs.title: API Key Authentication
docs.text:
Set the MIA_API_KEY environment variable to enable authentication:

export MIA_API_KEY=mia_api_your_secure_key_here

Provide the API key via: - Header: X-API-Key: <your-api-key> - Query Parameter: ?api_key=<your-api-key>

docs.text:
import requests

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
API_KEY = "your_api_key"

headers = {"X-API-Key": API_KEY}

# Get devices

print(response.json())

# Send command
response = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/command",
    headers=headers,
    json={
        "device": "gpio_worker_1",
        "action": "GPIO_SET",
        "params": {"pin": 18, "value": True}
    }
)
print(response.json())

docs.title: MQTT Topics (výběr)
docs.text:
• vehicle/telemetry/{vin}/obd – fuel, rpm, speed, coolant, dtc[]
  • vehicle/events/{vin}/anpr – plate_hash, confidence, snapshot_id

  • vehicle/cmd/{vin}/io – relé/LED/buzzer

Detailní popis viz spec/interfaces/topics.md.

docs.title: Flow: Telemetry → Alert → Command
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant ESP as ESP32
  participant AND as Android
  participant BRO as MQTT Broker
  participant IO as IO Node

  ESP->>AND: BLE Telemetry Notify (CBOR)
  AND->>BRO: Publish vehicle/telemetry/{vin}/obd
  AND->>AND: Evaluate rules (fuel_low,temp_high)
  AND->>BRO: Publish vehicle/alerts/{vin}
  AND->>BRO: Publish vehicle/cmd/{vin}/io {"buzzer":"short"}
  BRO-->>IO: Deliver IO command
